app.title: pyXLMS web app: convert, validate, filter and export crosslink search results
app.summary: A person uploads one or more result files from a crosslink search engine, says which engine and crosslinker made them, and can choose processing steps: re-annotating protein positions from a FASTA file, keeping unique matches, validating at a target FDR, keeping target matches only, and aggregating to crosslinks. The parsed crosslink-spectrum-matches and crosslinks are shown as tables with summary statistics. The person can then narrow them by protein accession, crosslink type and target-decoy type, look at distribution plots, and export the result in the input format of a chosen downstream tool, adding a FASTA or a structure file where that tool needs one.

task.text: Turn crosslink search engine output into validated, filtered, summarised results saved in the format a downstream analysis tool needs.

data.text: Tables of crosslink identifications from mass spectrometry search engines. Each row is a crosslink-spectrum-match or a crosslink linking two peptides, with sequences, crosslink positions, proteins, scores and decoy flags.
data.item: a crosslink-spectrum-match or crosslink: a pair of crosslinked peptides with their positions in proteins, a score and target/decoy labels

stage.text: cleaning and validating crosslink search results after the database search, before structural or network analysis in other tools

mechanism.text: Tabs run in pipeline order: Load Data, Filter, Visualize, Export. Each tab works on the same parsed result held in session state, and each filter or reload resets earlier exports. Every tab shows its current tables or plots and offers file downloads, and the export forms ask for whatever extra input the chosen target format needs.

workflow.name: convert a result table between tool formats after validating and filtering it

steps.here: upload one or more result files, choose the search engine or format and the crosslinker (or enter a custom name and mass), then press 'Read file(s)!'

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: optional toggles re-annotate protein positions from an uploaded FASTA, keep unique matches, validate at a target FDR with a chosen formula and concatenated or separate intra/inter FDR, keep target matches only, and aggregate to crosslinks grouped by peptide or by protein position

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: read crosslink-spectrum-matches, crosslinks and aggregated crosslinks appear as tables with a row of summary statistics, each downloadable as .csv, .xlsx or .json

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: a form keeps only chosen protein accessions, intra or inter crosslinks, and target-target, target-decoy or decoy-decoy matches, then shows the current tables
bar charts and histograms of target/decoy counts, scores, crosslink type, and the top-N proteins, peptide pairs and residue pairs, plus STRING scores for inter-links once an organism is chosen

pick a downstream tool (xiFDR, xiVIEW, xiNET, ProXL, AlphaLink2, PyXlinkViewer, xlms-tools, XMAS, XlinkDB, IMP-X-FDR, MS Annika), give any extra input it needs such as a FASTA or a PDB code or file, then download the converted file

distinctive: False discovery rate is estimated from target-decoy labels, with a choice of formula, of whether intra and inter links get separate FDRs, and of whether higher or lower scores are better
Results exist at three levels (spectrum matches, crosslinks, aggregated crosslinks), and each tab handles each level on its own
Before exporting, the app checks that every field the target tool needs is present, and some exports also need a FASTA or a protein structure file so positions can be mapped to chains
Inter-links can be annotated with protein interaction scores from the online STRING database for a chosen organism
Peptides in each pair are reordered into a canonical alpha/beta order so that duplicate crosslinks can be found

parts.title: Load Data tab
parts.summary: Uploads search engine result files, takes the engine and crosslinker, and parses them into spectrum matches and crosslinks.

parts.title: Processing options
parts.summary: Toggles and fields for re-annotating positions, keeping unique matches, FDR validation, target-only filtering and aggregation, applied when the files are read.

parts.title: Read results with summary statistics
parts.summary: Shows the parsed spectrum matches, crosslinks and aggregated crosslinks as tables with summary counts, and offers each one as a .csv, .xlsx or .json download.

parts.title: Filter tab
parts.summary: Keeps only matches with chosen proteins, crosslink types and target-decoy types, then shows and offers the current tables for download.

parts.title: Visualize tab
parts.summary: Lays out distribution plots of target/decoy counts, scores, crosslink types, top proteins, peptide pairs, residue pairs and STRING scores, with set bin counts and top-N.

parts.title: Export tab
parts.summary: Picks a downstream tool for each result level, explains what that tool needs, converts the data and offers the file for download.

parts.title: Export onto a protein structure
parts.summary: Takes a PDB code or structure file, maps crosslink positions onto chains and downloads the files a molecular viewer needs, along with the sequence-mapping metadata.
